objective: Evaluating initial AI feasibility: technical viability, data availability/quality, computational resource requirements, and organizational readiness
secondaryObjectives: Conducting risk assessments across security, safety, and ethics: failure modes, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and mitigation strategies
Managing adoption and integration risk: change-management requirements, user-resistance planning, and training strategies

sources.cite: PMI Certified Professional in Managing AI (PMI-CPMAI) Examination Content Outline (September 2025): Responsible and Trustworthy AI 15%, Business Needs and Solutions 26%, Data Needs 26%, Model Development and Evaluation 16%, Operationalize 17%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's syllabus page that restates the outline in its own words (PMI's PDF did not come up in search). Restated: data evaluation (assess data quality; analyze distributions for bias or gaps; exploratory data analysis); model governance (lifecycle management, versioning and change control, monitor performance and detect drift). The objective wording here is the course seed's; PMI's own wording is to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's loan-data-bias-pmicpmai (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You manage AI projects at a fictional utility, Brennan Power. The COO wants an AI that routes customer calls and flags customers in vulnerable circumstances for priority help.
handover: Two years of call transcripts exist; vulnerability flags were recorded inconsistently.
Agents fear the AI will be used to monitor them.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the vendor's vulnerability model, trained on sparse labels, misses most vulnerable customers in testing.
Week 3: in the pilot, callers with strong accents are routed to the wrong queue three times as often; complaints follow.
Week 4: agents stop overriding wrong routes to avoid scrutiny; vulnerable callers wait longer.

feasPrompt.title: Can it be done?
feasPrompt.context: The COO wants both features in one release.

choices.label: Assess both: routing is feasible on existing data; vulnerability detection is not yet (labels too poor); propose routing first and a labelling effort

effects.log: A scoped, feasible plan is proposed.

choices.feedback: Feasibility covers data, technology, compute and readiness; commit to what's viable.

choices.label: Commit to both and hope labels improve
choices.feedback: The vulnerability model can't be trained well on these labels.

choices.label: Skip feasibility: the vendor says it works

riskPrompt.title: What could go wrong?
riskPrompt.context: Routing errors could send vulnerable customers to long queues.

choices.label: Assess failure modes (misrouting vulnerable callers), security (transcript access), ethics (bias against accents) with mitigations: human override, access controls, bias testing
choices.feedback: AI risk assessment covers failure modes, security and ethics, with mitigations before launch.

choices.label: Assess security only
choices.feedback: Safety and ethics risks are missed.

choices.label: Skip it: routing is low risk
choices.feedback: Misrouting vulnerable callers is a safety risk.

adoptPrompt.title: Agents fear surveillance
adoptPrompt.context: Agents may work around the system.

choices.label: A change plan: tell agents what the AI does and doesn't do (no performance monitoring, in writing), involve them in testing, train them, and use their cues to improve labels
choices.feedback: Adoption needs change management: transparency, involvement and training.

choices.label: Mandate use and track overrides per agent
choices.feedback: Tracking overrides per agent confirms the surveillance fear.

reflection.question: Write the go/no-go recommendation for the COO.

parts.label: Feasibility
parts.criteria: Routing feasible; vulnerability labels missing in 70%; labelling first.
parts.modelAnswer: Routing is feasible on our transcripts; vulnerability detection isn't until labels improve, so we start with routing and a labelling effort.

parts.label: Risk and adoption
parts.criteria: Failure modes, security and bias mitigated; change plan with agents.
parts.modelAnswer: We mitigate misrouting with human override, restrict transcript access and test for accent bias; agents are involved and promised no monitoring.

scoring.modelReasoning: Before committing to an AI solution, evaluate feasibility (data availability and quality, technology, compute, organizational readiness), assess risks across security, safety and ethics with mitigations, and plan adoption through change management, involvement and training.
